segments.text: Good morning, everyone. In today's talk, we will discuss dreams.
I believe none of you here could possibly say you've never had a dream.
You may forget what your dream was about, but you cannot deny the fact that you had a dream.
Let's begin with a few fun facts about dreams.
dreams. Believe it or not, you dream between 3 and 6 times per night, and each dream lasts
between 5 to 20 minutes. The reason why you find that first fact hard to believe is that
about 95% of dreams are forgotten by the time you get out of bed.
So what are dreams? The most common definition is that dreams are stories and images that
our minds create while we sleep. They can be anything from entertaining, fun, romantic,
disturbing, frightening, and sometimes bizarre. A more scientific way to define dreams is
that they are a universal human experience that can be described as a state of consciousness
characterized by sensory, cognitive, and emotional occurrences during sleep.
Dreams can happen at any time during sleep, but you have your most vivid dreams during
a phase called REM, or rapid eye movement, which is the phase of sleep when your brain
is most active.
We will talk about the phases of sleep at a different time.
Right, so why do dreams occur?
There are several theories about why we dream, but no one knows for sure.
Some researchers say dreams have no purpose or meaning.
Others say we need dreams for our mental, emotional, and physical health.
In one study, researchers woke people just as they were going into REM sleep.
They found that those who weren't allowed to dream had more tension, they developed
anxiety and depression, gained weight, and lacked coordination and concentration.
Many experts say that dreams exist to help solve problems in our lives, incorporate
memories and process emotions.
It means if you go to bed with a troubling thought, you may wake with a solution or
at least feel better about the situation.
But remember not to rely on dreams as a way to solve problems.
I've seen many people end up sleeping all day and their problems are still haunting
them in their sleep.
The next question is, do dreams have any meaning?
Or is it just your brain using random images to mess with you?
Just as there are different opinions about why we dream, there are different views about
what dreams mean.
Some experts say dreams have no connection to our real emotions or thoughts.
They're just strange stories that don't relate to normal life.
Others say our dreams may reflect our own thoughts and feelings.
deepest desires, fears, and concerns, especially dreams that happen over and over. By interpreting
our dreams, we may gain insight into our lives and ourselves. Many people say they've come
up with their best ideas while dreaming. Often, people report having similar dreams.
They're being chased, fall off a cliff, or show up in public naked. These types
of dreams are probably caused by hidden stress or anxiety.
The dreams may be similar, but experts say the meaning behind the dream is unique to
each person.
Before we round up what we've learned today about dreams, I'd like to talk about a study
I find interesting on the characters that appear in our dreams.
In this study, researchers asked 320 candidates to identify the people they met in their
dreams.
They found that 48% of characters represented a named person known to the dreamer, 35% of
characters were identified by their social role, for example a policeman, or their relationship
to the dreamer, such as a friend, and 16% were not recognized.
Among the characters that the candidates could name, 32% were identified by appearance, 21%
behavior, 45% by face, and 44% by sense.
Well, that's it for today.
